title: Names and family origins
description: Connie Richard identifies Marie Smith by her nickname and real name, then records her birth in Moscow, her maiden name Zagelow, and her parents' names. Marie describes her mother's work in a match factory and housekeeping, her father's job as a master mechanic for PFI, and her two brothers.

title: Marriage, husband, and children
description: Marie identifies her husband Lesley, his work as a machine operator for Potlatch, their 1962 marriage, and the births of their four children. She also discusses her education, sewing and baking interests, earlier office and volunteer work, and local clubs she belongs to in Bovill.

title: Small-town life and childhood
description: Marie compares rural and urban life, saying Bovill offers small schools, close neighbors, and greater freedom for children. She recalls childhood bike riding, swimming, Cub Scouts, a girls' club, and a small log cabin playhouse.

title: Dating and marriage decisions
description: Marie describes high school dances, ball games, and meeting Lesley through school before dating him in their teens. She explains that they married young after he got better Potlatch work and reflects on their expectations about children and married life.

title: Mike's diagnosis and therapy
description: Marie explains that Mike was not diagnosed with cerebral palsy until he was two and that local doctors delayed answers. She describes therapy in Moscow and at WSU, the Boise rehabilitation program, foster care, typing with assistance, and Mike's effort to write a book about his life.

title: Family size, religion, and support networks
description: Marie says her children were unplanned and explains how Catholic teaching affected her use of birth control until a priest allowed pills. She discusses learning about childbirth from her mother and school, then describes parent groups in Lewiston and the lack of services, trained doctors, and recreational options for disabled children.

title: Children's futures and family work
description: Marie hopes her children will get further education or training and avoid woods work because of layoffs and limited opportunity. She talks about family recreation, babysitting, canning, sewing, and how she might support the family if something happened to her husband.

title: Volunteer work and community needs
description: Marie lists volunteer work for the Cancer Society, Fireman's Auxiliary, school classrooms, and community events. She says Bovill needs more industry beyond lumber and briefly discusses county fairs and advice for young women in small towns.

title: Adjusting to town life and local resources
description: Marie recalls being lonelier in Lewiston than in Bovill and advises newcomers to join clubs and meet people. She describes welcoming practices, newspapers, Reader's Digest, the Bookmobile, and the family's television viewing.

title: Household decisions; reasons for staying
description: Marie says she and her husband discuss major purchases, job changes, and child discipline together. She explains that they stay in Bovill because they like small-town life, neighbors help during medical crises, insurance matters, and Lesley's work is tied to the timber industry.
